description: We are a group of students with a passion to build, to tinker and mess about with things we know and don't.
summary:
Across years of evolution it is curiosity that has set human beings apart, their tendency of asking why, sometimes even at the cost of their own lives is what has led to all the scientific discoveries and revelations we see and use in our day to day life. 
Which is why we CurioCET present project Luna to prepare the future generation for a day that will surely come to pass. 
The year is 2047 and you are the captain of Luna, the experimental venture set up by NASA to lead the first extraterrestrial outpost on the Moon. But it isn't easy to just run an outpost, you need to monitor power, oxygen, water and a thousands of other factors and then there are events like solar flares adding in to chaos.
What will you do? Being unsuccessful in one mission could affect the chances of others too, will humanity be able to survive in these harsh conditions? 
It's all up to you. Your decisions will define the future of mankind.

The project code is at: https://github.com/Joseph-mappila/NASA-SPACE-APPS/
The actual game is at: https://joseph-mappila.github.io/NASA-SPACE-APPS/
details:
Our project is Luna, an interactive game like experience to educate students about astronauts and procedures at NASA while being a fun source of pastime and fun.

From the start humanity has set themselves apart by being curious, by asking questions, by seeking for answers no matter how hard the universe tries to hide it from us. This perseverance for seeking the truth is what sets us apart and has enabled us to discover scientific innovations and revelations that power the modern society.

It's the year 2047, humanity has finally managed to stop being confined to the tiny speck of dust that is Earth and established it's first extraterrestrial outpost at the Moon. But not all is easy on the lunar surface, there's a lot of problems arising here and there and a solar storm is due soon, the fate of humankind rests on the captain and the crew, will they manage to pull off the mission and continue running the outpost?

Our project prioritises realism, we want young learners to understand that their actions can have significant impact on the survival of the outpost, that is why we used realistic minigames that explain actual NASA procedure followed when problems arise and need to be resolved, albeit making sure it's simpler and more visual.

This ensures that learners have an understanding of how NASA uses science in the real world to get things done, from cleaning a simple solar panel, to securing against a solar storm, we used realistic graphical visualisations to make students understand how things work behind the scenes to educate them on a reality that's bound to come by. To bring up the future generation of astronauts that will take us to the moon and beyond.

Visuals and readups from the actual NASA website are also provided for the curious learners who want to know more about how things actually work behind the scenes.

For the tech stack we used:

  • React 19 and TypeScript
  • Vite 7
  • GSAP ScrollTrigger for the opening sequence
  • Web Audio API for generated sound effects and scene ambience
  • Hand-written SVG for the scenes and CSS for the interface
  • Vitest and Testing Library
  • NASA public APIs: DONKI, EPIC, TechPort, Image and Video Library, POWER, JPL Horizons, NeoWs, InSight, and Worldview (GIBS)
  • GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages

No special hardware is needed: the game runs in any modern browser on a laptop, tablet, or phone. There is no game engine, no backend, and no database. The three supplied character and environment illustrations are the only images bundled with the project; NASA photos load from NASA's image servers.

The project code is at: https://github.com/Joseph-mappila/NASA-SPACE-APPS/

The actual game is at: https://joseph-mappila.github.io/NASA-SPACE-APPS/
